key_insight: The paper proposes that defect-assisted absorption of room-temperature infrared self-emission contributes to Zener breakdown and ohmic behavior in heavily doped p–n junctions alongside quantum tunneling.
engineering_relevance: If validated, this mechanism could inform modeling of heavily doped semiconductor contacts and reverse-bias behavior, though the abstract demonstrates no AI or solar-cell application.
method: Propose sub-band-gap carrier generation through defect-assisted absorption of self-emitted infrared photons.
Attribute reverse leakage to collection of these carriers by the junction’s built-in field.
Invoke low-voltage avalanche multiplication and combine the proposed photovoltaic mechanism with tunneling.
evidence_signal: The abstract offers a conceptual explanation, including qualitative temperature-dependence arguments, but reports no measurements, simulations, or quantitative comparisons.
watch_item: The proposal must establish consistency with thermal detailed balance and distinguish any self-emission contribution from established tunneling, thermal-generation, and avalanche mechanisms.
paper_title: Mechanisms of Zener diode and ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction: A novel explanation in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect resulting from infrared self-emission at room-temperature
